title: Ireland Stun Reigning World Champions India With Historic 2-0 T20I Sweep
excerpt: Three months after lifting the T20 World Cup, Shreyas Iyer's new-look India were humbled at Stormont as Rajasthan-born debutant Jai Moondra inspired Ireland to their first series win over India in any format.
body:
• Ireland beat India 2-0 at Belfast — a 34-run win on June 26 and a one-run thriller on June 28 — for their first-ever series victory over India in any format.
  • The sweep ended India's 16-series unbeaten run in T20I cricket and spoiled Shreyas Iyer's first assignment as India's new T20I captain.
  • Rajasthan-born seamer Jai Moondra, on international debut, was Player of the Series with five wickets, including 3/32 in the decider.
  • The defeat came just three months after India retained the T20 World Cup, making it one of the biggest upsets in recent T20I history.

A stunning sweep at Stormont

Ireland completed a historic 2-0 T20I series sweep over India at the Civil Service Cricket Club at Stormont in Belfast, humbling the reigning world champions on consecutive evenings. On June 26, Ireland posted 182 for 9 and bowled India out for 148 to win by 34 runs. Two days later Ireland defended 154 to win by a single run, with India stranded on 153 for 9. The results were India's first defeats to Ireland in any format and ended the visitors' 16-series winning streak in T20Is.

A new era begins badly

The tour was supposed to mark the start of a new cycle. In March, India had thrashed New Zealand by 96 runs in the T20 World Cup final at Ahmedabad — becoming the first team to defend the title and the first to lift the trophy three times. On June 6, chief selector Ajit Agarkar unveiled a squad built for the 2028 cycle: Shreyas Iyer was named T20I captain, with Suryakumar Yadav — the World Cup-winning captain — dropped from the setup altogether. Tilak Varma became vice-captain, and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was picked after his 776-run IPL 2026 season earned him the Orange Cap.

"We debated it a lot, not the easiest discussion especially if you've won the World Cup," Agarkar said of the decision to move on from Suryakumar Yadav. Ireland were led by Lorcan Tucker and had lost all eight previous meetings with India.

How the sweep happened

In the first T20I, India won the toss and bowled, but Lorcan Tucker (50 off 35) and Gareth Delany (50 off 31) lifted Ireland to 182 for 9. Debutant Jai Moondra dismissed Sanju Samson with his first ball in international cricket as India were bowled out for 148.

The second game was tighter and crueler. Harry Tector's 53 off 47 anchored Ireland's 154 for 8, with Prince Yadav taking 3/22 for India. Tilak Varma fought alone with 55 off 46, but Moondra struck again — 3/32, removing Samson for a golden duck for the second day running, along with Abhishek Sharma and captain Iyer. India fell one run short as Moondra's 3/32 headlined the defence.

"Still trying to sink in the feeling. I know it's hard to describe in one word. It's an amazing feeling playing against the best, testing yourself."

— Jai Moondra, after being named Player of the Match and Player of the Series

What the result means

For India, the sweep put immediate pressure on the new regime. Iyer's captaincy began with two defeats, and the decision to discard a World Cup-winning captain invited scrutiny. Without Bumrah and the senior core, India's attack looked mortal on a Belfast surface where runs were hard to come by, and the batting collapsed in clusters in both chases.

For Ireland it was a first series win over India in any format — and the breakout already has commercial weight: Moondra was picked first overall by the Rotterdam Dockers in the inaugural European T20 Premier League draft, with co-owner Jonty Rhodes calling him "an exciting young talent with tremendous potential."

The Rajasthan-to-Dublin journey

The hero of the series wore green, but his story began in Tonk, Rajasthan. Born in 1997, Jai Moondra earned a B.Tech from SRM Institute in Chennai before moving to Dublin in 2021 for an M.Sc at Technological University Dublin. He worked nearly three years as a product development engineer at Intel while playing domestic cricket for Leinster — then left the corporate job in June 2025 to chase cricket full-time.

His mother Vidya Moondra told ANI she was saddened by India's defeat but proud of her son bringing fame to the family, Rajasthan and the nation. For the Indian diaspora in Ireland — and millions watching back home — the series had a familiar face on the other side of an unfamiliar result.

What's next

India moved on to the England leg of their tour, and Belfast will be remembered as the place where the new India learned how quickly world cricket is catching up.
image_caption: India's players celebrate with the trophy after winning the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final against New Zealand at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. Three months later, the world champions were swept 2-0 by Ireland at Belfast.
nri_angle: Jai Moondra, born in Tonk, Rajasthan and a former Intel engineer, starred for Ireland against his birth country — a storyline that resonated with the Indian diaspora in Ireland and fans back home.
